overview: Colour of the seed The seeds are either yellow or green colour. The trait expressed in F1 generation is called dominant. In F2 generation about 75% seeds were with dominant character (Eg: Yellow seeds) and about 25% seeds were with recessive character (Eg: Green seeds).

vsaq.question: Complete the key idea: Colour of the seed The seeds are either _____ or green colour.
vsaq.answer: Colour of the seed The seeds are either yellow or green colour.

vsaq.question: Complete the key idea: The trait expressed in F1 _____ is called dominant.
vsaq.answer: The trait expressed in F1 generation is called dominant.

vsaq.question: Complete the key idea: These small changes within the species for example _____ of beetles red and green is known as ‘Micro evolution’.
vsaq.answer: These small changes within the species for example colour of beetles red and green is known as ‘Micro evolution’.

vsaq.question: Complete the key idea: Mendel believed that every character or trait is controlled or responsible by a pair of _____.
vsaq.answer: Mendel believed that every character or trait is controlled or responsible by a pair of factors.

vsaq.question: Complete the key idea: Transmission or passing of characters or _____ from parent to offsprings is called ‘Heredity’.
vsaq.answer: Transmission or passing of characters or traits from parent to offsprings is called ‘Heredity’.

vsaq.question: Complete the key idea: _____ are passed from parent to offspring through heredity.
vsaq.answer: Variations are passed from parent to offspring through heredity.

vsaq.question: Complete the key idea: A pure breed (parental) _____ seed producing pea will also have both the ‘factors’ of the same type.
vsaq.answer: A pure breed (parental) green seed producing pea will also have both the ‘factors’ of the same type.

vsaq.question: Complete the key idea: So they were able to generate variations in _____.
vsaq.answer: So they were able to generate variations in population.

vsaq.question: Complete the key idea: The determining agent _____ for each trait is called a factor.
vsaq.answer: The determining agent responsible for each trait is called a factor.

vsaq.question: Complete the key idea: The _____ expressed in F1 is dominant, not expressed is recessive.
vsaq.answer: The trait expressed in F1 is dominant, not expressed is recessive.

saq.question: Explain similarity and world with reference to Heredity - Evolution.
saq.answer: When we observe our world and its myriad forms of life, we are struck by two seemingly opposite observations, the fantastic variety of life and the similarity between them. As we shall see, we would need to understand these two characteristics of life in order to comprehend how life evolves.

saq.question: Explain reproductive and reproduction with reference to Heredity - Evolution.
saq.answer: In the chapter on reproduction we have studied that reproductive processes usually give rise to individuals that have some new characters in spite of the similarity that they share with their parents. Often such new characters give rise to observable changes in life forms.

saq.question: Explain variations and characters with reference to Heredity - Evolution.
saq.answer: Differences in characters within very closely related groups of organisms are referred to as variations. Often a new character in a group may lead to variations which also get inherited.
